title: Variables
explain: Variables are containers that store data values in Python. You create a variable by choosing a name and using the equals sign (=) to assign a value to it. Variable names should be descriptive and can contain letters, numbers, and underscores (but cannot start with a number).
code:
# Create variables
name = "Alice"
age = 25
height = 5.8
is_student = True

# Use variables
print("Name:", name)
print("Age:", age)
print("Height:", height)
print("Is student:", is_student)
exercise: Create three variables: one storing your favorite color (text), one storing your lucky number (whole number), and one storing your height in meters (decimal). Then print all three.
tip: A common mistake is forgetting that variable names are case-sensitive: 'age' and 'Age' are two different variables. Also, don't use Python keywords (like 'for', 'if', 'class') as variable names.
